If you have a tap open and flush your toilet at the same time it still works, as the waste water is heavier and flows on the bottom of the pipe, and the clean water flows at the top. I would recommend checking out bodybuilding.com. Excellent FAQs and over a decade of forums to peruse.

As far as your routine - without going into too much detail I'd recommend dead lifts and bench presses. These should be staples, even for bodybuilders. You can only get so far doing isolation movements. And not very far, at that.

The results aren't going to come fast. I'm assuming you're young, so your body can take a good amount of volume, but one of the biggest mistakes young people make with weight training is too much, too fast.

As to your question - you can train if you're sore but soreness is something that really should only be happening when you first start or change routines. Being sore after every workout isn't normal. Settle into a routine. 3, 4 days a week. Consistency is more important than anything. And keep eating a lot!
